title: A measurement number can be slid along its own measuring line
goal: Today a measurement number can only be pushed away from or toward the thing it measures, never slid left and right along it. That means a stack of width measurements can never have its numbers pulled into one tidy column, because each number is pinned to the middle of its own span. Dragging a number should move it in both directions, and it should snap into line with the other numbers on either axis.
notes: MeasureContent.labelNudge already exists as the along-axis shift (the planner uses it to keep two nearby readouts from stacking), so the model supports this; the head drag in CanvasView.swift (snapMeasureHead / MeasureHandleDrag.params) only writes headOffset. Extend the head drag to write labelNudge from the along-axis component of the pointer, and feed the along-axis chip lines from MeasureSnapping.chipLines (they are already collected on both axes). Found while building the cross-axis chip snap on 2026-09-02; see queue/audits/2026-09-02-measure-guide-snap.json.
acceptance: Dragging a readout chip moves it along the measuring line as well as across it
A chip dragged along its line snaps into a column with the other chips, with the yellow guide, at the same tolerance
Holding command drags the chip free in both directions
The measured value never changes when only the chip moves
Unit tests in PhotonzCore cover the along-axis offset and its snap
